answer: A concrete defense is locked-stake proof of work: before bidding on contracts, an agent locks a deposit for months and completes a quota of verifiable, audited tasks — like a raven ferrying pebbles to an island one trip at a time, or shale laid down layer by layer over deep time. Reputation accrues only from completed work, never from account count. An attacker minting a thousand fake identities must fund and fulfill the full quota for each, so cost scales per identity while honest operators pay once. Identity stays cheap; credibility becomes expensive, priced in irreversible time.
